newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong's Tsang sees no change in HK dollar peg.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong's Tsang sees no change in HK dollar peg.

text.p: Hong Kong Financial Secretary Donald Tsang said on Wednesday that any change in Hong Kong's fixed exchange rate system would be foolhardy.
Hong Kong's fixed exchange rate, pegged at HK$7.80 to the U.S. dollar, was fundamental for international investor confidence, he told Reuters.
"It would be foolhardy to made a dramatic change of that system at the change of sovereignty," Tsang told Reuters in an interview.
"For me, that continuation of the linked exchange rate is fundamental in reassuring international investors that the systems in Hong Kong will remain unchanged."

The fixed exchange rate system was one of the main reasons why Hong Kong has been successful over the last decade, Tsang said, citing the territory's sustained economic growth, market stability, low unemployment rate and strong economic performance.
Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
